video_title: 2026 Training Camp Media Availability | Coach J.B. Bickerstaff l 10.06.26

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff on the rookie's intelligence and emotional poise
quotes.excerpt: he's highly intelligent, he understands the game, he can run a show
quotes.quote: He's a good player. He's highly intelligent, he understands the game, he can run a show, having the ball in his hands, he can put people in the right spots. He's tough and gritty defensively, and emotionally he always stays poised. You don't see him doing the up and down, so I think that's going to help him in his rookie year.
quotes.social_post: J.B. Bickerstaff is impressed with his rookie's poise and basketball IQ early in camp, noting that he is highly intelligent and always stays poised, which will help him in his rookie year.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: Benefits of playing multiple ball-handlers simultaneously
quotes.excerpt: being able to have multiple ball-handlers on the floor, multiple guys who can play at the point
quotes.quote: It depends on how teams are playing us, obviously, but being able to have multiple ball-handlers on the floor, multiple guys who can play at the point of attack, break their man down, get to the paint, create for others, just makes everybody else on the floor better.
quotes.social_post: Coach Bickerstaff on the Pistons offensive philosophy: having multiple ball handlers on the floor who can break down defenses and create for others makes everyone else better.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: Early training camp assessment of the rookie's development
quotes.excerpt: he's done a great job of picking up the things that we've been introducing
quotes.quote: He's done a great job of picking up the things that we've been introducing. His cutting has been really good, his moving off the ball has been really good, his shot-making obviously, and his defense has improved from last year also. So, he's had a good first week.
quotes.social_post: J.B. Bickerstaff says his rookie has had a strong first week of training camp, specifically highlighting improvements in his off-ball movement and defensive intensity.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: How the rookie can earn rotation minutes in preseason
quotes.excerpt: he's got an opportunity to earn minutes through preseason
quotes.quote: It's difficult obviously with just the amount of guys we have, but he's got an opportunity to earn minutes through preseason, and doing the things that we just talked about is how he earns minutes. Taking the step which I believe he has defensively, being able to pick the ball up in the backcourt, his off-ball defense, because we know he can make shots, but we want him to be an impactful player on both ends of the floor, and he's proving that he can do that.
quotes.social_post: Bickerstaff says his rookie has a clear path to earning rotation minutes this preseason by proving he can be an impactful player on both ends of the floor, specifically through his defensive effort.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: Creating floor spacing through gravity and perimeter threats
quotes.excerpt: the gravity that they have, and then that creates openings for everybody else
quotes.quote: It's obviously the gravity that they have, and then that creates openings for everybody else, whether you're playing the pick and roll or you're driving to the basket. People are less likely to help off those guys that they know are knockdown shooters, so it just creates that spacing. Especially if we can get out in transition and get to those spots early, now you got full-court threat and the ability to attack and get to the paint, it just creates that space that you're looking for.
quotes.social_post: Bickerstaff explains the importance of gravity in the Pistons offense, noting that having knockdown shooters creates the spacing needed to attack the paint and generate open looks.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: Veteran leadership and mentorship of younger players
quotes.excerpt: he grabs the young guys all the time, and he's having conversations with the young guys
quotes.quote: He's a pro, he's a veteran, he's one of our most vocal guys. I love watching him because he grabs the young guys all the time, and he's having conversations with the young guys all the time. Even at halftime last night where some of the young guys hadn't played, he grabbed them, asked them what they were doing to stay locked in, how they were going to be focused when they got their opportunity. So it's great to have a veteran who can do that and can play.
quotes.social_post: J.B. Bickerstaff praises his veteran players for their leadership, noting that they are constantly grabbing young guys to keep them locked in and focused even when they are not in the rotation.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of a positive veteran presence in the locker room
quotes.excerpt: he's enjoyable to be around all the time. He's got a great positive spirit, great energy
quotes.quote: He is that way. He's enjoyable to be around all the time. He's got a great positive spirit, great energy, so he fits in with the group because we have a bunch of guys like that. It just makes everybody's job easier and it makes him a better player because he knows who he is, he's confident in who he is, and knows how he impacts winning.
quotes.social_post: Bickerstaff on the importance of locker room culture, saying that having players with a positive spirit and energy makes everyone's job easier and helps them understand how to impact winning.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: Adjusting defensive schemes to account for mid-range threats
quotes.excerpt: people are going to have to make an adjustment on how they defend him
quotes.quote: People are going to have to make an adjustment on how they defend him, and spacing can be created in so many different ways. If he's making that mid-range pull-up, it's still spacing. I know people get caught up in the analytics of it, but his ability to make that shot changes the way teams have to guard him when he has the ball in his hand, and even when he doesn't. So the confidence to take that shot is something he's been working on, and he's continued to get better at it.
quotes.social_post: Bickerstaff defends the mid-range game, noting that a player's ability to hit that shot changes how teams have to guard them and creates necessary spacing regardless of analytics.
